label: UniFi Dream Machine (UDM)
description: Ubiquiti UniFi Dream Machine - all-in-one security gateway, 4-port managed Gigabit switch and dual-band 802.11ac Wave 2 access point in one chassis. 5x GbE RJ45 (1 WAN + 4 LAN), 4x4 MU-MIMO on 5 GHz, 2.4 GHz 802.11n, 1 Gbps IDS/IPS throughput, 26 W maximum draw from an internal AC/DC adapter.
notes: The page states the wiring twice over ('5 GbE Ports: 1 WAN and 4 LAN', then '4 x LAN 10/100/1000 RJ45 Ports, 1 x WAN 10/100/1000 RJ45 Port'), so the split is quoted, not inferred: exactly one WAN socket and four LAN sockets in one bridge group. Per-band radio rates (300 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, 1.7 Gbps on 5 GHz) are the class rates for 802.11n 2.4 GHz and 4x4 802.11ac Wave 2; the page states the radio classes but no PHY rate, so the numbers are the class convention and are not presented as a quoted figure. Power is an internal AC/DC adapter at 26 W with no PoE in or out, which is why no `poeIn` is declared - a lab cannot power this over the LAN cable. Power is the important silence: the page gives an internal AC/DC adapter and 26 W with no PoE-in, so every RJ45 port declares `poeIn: 0` rather than leaving it out. Left out, the engine's access-point heuristic (any model or label containing "UniFi") would infer 12.95 W on each port and then warn that a PC cannot feed it - a wattage no datasheet claims, on a box that plugs into the wall.
